sentences.text: The appellant/claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988 and Rule 3 of M.A.C.T claiming compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- for the injuries caused him in the road accident on 20.09.2016.

3. The learned Tribunal after hearing both sides and upon considering the oral and documentary evidence has granted compensation Rs.1,60,800/- in the following manner:-

5. The appellant/claimant, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal,, has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
6. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

7. The learned counsel for the appellant has raised the following grounds:-
(i) The learned Judge erred in holding that the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation except Rs.1,60,800/- as liability against the claim amount of Rs.8,00,000/-
(ii) The learned Judge failed to consider that the petitioner was inpatient for around one month in ESI Hospital, inpatient for one day in parvathy Hospita, and also he was taking treatment as out-patient till the ende of 2019 as per the discharge summaries marked as Ex.P4 & P5.

(iii) The learned Judge failed to consider that the petitioner is a lorry driver and having heavy vehicle licence and erred not in considering he employment of the petitioner and thereby fixed the salary of the petitioner as Rs.11,000/- per month as the notional income of the petitioner.
In fact, the learned Judge failed to consider the driving license of the petitioner marked as Ex.P8 to prove the avocation of the petitioner.

Therefore, the learned Judge erred in fixing the earning of the petitioner as Rs.11,000/-
per month , even thought the earning of the petitioner is https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

(
Uploaded on: 09/06/2025 05:24:56 pm ) Rs.30,000/- per month.
He further submitted that the award passed by the Tribunal under all the heads is lower, which requires interference by this Court and prays to allow this appeal.

8. The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal taking into consideration all the relevant documents has rightly fixed the compensation, which does not require any interference.
Hence, he prayed for dismissal of this appeal.
9. In the instant case, the Injured person is a driver and he loss for income.
The accident had taken place in the year 2014.
However, the loss of income of the appellant was fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.11,000/- which is on the lower side.
Hence, he is driver by profession, hence this Court is inclined to increase the loss of income Rs.18,000x3= Rs.54,000/-
Further, the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and sufferings & mental agony which is on the lower side and the same is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-
